author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory page lists each specialty with its veterinarians
summary: A page at its own address lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians who hold it shown by full name (first name then last name), all on one page with no paging. It lists specialties, not the full veterinarian roster.
acceptance_criteria: Given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened at its address, then every specialty is listed by its stored name, each with the veterinarians who hold it shown by full name (first name then last name).
Given a veterinarian who holds no specialty, when the directory is opened, then that veterinarian does not appear on the page.
Given the clinic's specialties, when the directory is opened, then all of them appear on one page, with no paging control.
Given the directory, when the surface is surveyed, then it is reachable only by its own address, with no navigation entry and no link from another page pointing to it.
Given a specialty held by no veterinarian, when the directory is opened, then it is still listed and shown as held by none (narrowest reading of 'every specialty'; flagged open).
non_goals: NG-2: managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application stays out of scope; the page only reads and presents the stored collection.
A visible entry point (navigation entry or inbound link) is out of this slice and named as a possible follow-up.
notes: New REQ minted; the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 slot is not reused. Distinct from REQ-VET-001 (veterinarian-centric, paginated) which inverts the axis and stays unchanged. Three open questions carry narrowest-reading working assumptions (see docs/prd.md Open Questions): (1) exact stable order of specialties and of veterinarians within each — narrowest reading is a stable deterministic order, exact key undecided; (2) a specialty held by no veterinarian is listed and shown as held by none; (3) no visible entry point in this slice.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Read-only server-rendered directory that replicates the existing VetController + Thymeleaf pattern (system-design.md#contracts, templates/vets/vetList.html) with the vet/specialty axis inverted. No new module, no service layer, no new dependency, no new persistence pattern. The one adjustment beyond the existing pattern: to satisfy 'every specialty including those held by no vet', the complete Specialty set must be read directly from the specialties table, not derived from vet.getSpecialties() (which only surfaces held specialties). Per the prd-entry file_targets this is a new explicit @Query method on VetRepository (keeping repository count minimal, consistent with the codebase's no-PetRepository/no-VisitRepository tendency), not a new SpecialtyRepository. system-design.md updated: new SpecialtyController contract row; VetRepository and Specialty rows gain REQ-SPC-001.
integration_points: New route GET /specialties.html mapped by SpecialtyController (mirrors VetController's @GetMapping('/vets.html')); returns view name 'specialties/specialtyList'.

New VetRepository query method returning the full Collection<Specialty> via an explicit @Query('SELECT s FROM Specialty s'); Vet-Specialty ManyToMany is owned by Vet, so Specialty has no back-reference and the complete list cannot be reached through Vet.
SpecialtyController groups holders per specialty by inverting vet.getSpecialties() over vetRepository.findAll() (already cached), then pairs each specialty from the full set with its holder list.

Model hands the template specialties in a stable order, each with its holders in a stable order (e.g. a name-ordered LinkedHashMap<Specialty,List<Vet>>, or a small view type); ordering computed in Java, not in the template.
Template reuses the full-name expression ${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName} from vetList.html and the #{none} 'held by none' idiom.

patterns.description: Controller shape to mirror: @Controller, constructor-injected VetRepository, @GetMapping returning a feature-grouped view name. Drop the pagination helpers — REQ-SPC-001 is explicitly single-page, no paging.
Table/th:each and full-name rendering to mirror; drop the totalPages pagination block entirely (AC3).

Existing stable-order precedent: getSpecialties() sorts by NamedEntity::getName. Order specialties by stored name; order veterinarians within each by last name then first name — resolves Open Question 1 with a deterministic key consistent with PetTypeRepository name-ordering.

risks.risk: REQ-LANG-002 build test walks templates and requires every message key present in all 11 locale bundles. A hard-coded string or a new key added to only messages.properties fails the build.
risks.mitigation: Reuse existing keys — #{specialties}, #{vets} (='Veterinarians'), #{name}, #{none} all already exist and cover the headings/columns/empty case. If a genuinely new key is unavoidable, add it to every messages*.properties bundle.

risks.risk: AC4 requires the page reachable by its address alone — no nav entry, no inbound link. fragments/layout.html carries the site nav.
risks.mitigation: Do NOT edit fragments/layout.html or any nav/link; the visible entry point is the named follow-up, out of this slice. Guardrail, not a task.

risks.risk: Testing tension: existing VetControllerTests uses @WebMvcTest + @MockitoBean, which contradicts the project no-mocks / real-I-O testing policy (CLAUDE.md, testing-principles.md). The implementer/test-designer must pick a lane for SpecialtyControllerTests rather than copy the mock-based pattern by reflex.
risks.mitigation: Design-neutral; defer to testing-principles.md. Note the page reads seeded data (radiology/surgery/dentistry all held in the seed), so a mock-free @SpringBootTest slice against H2 aligns with the no-mocks policy; not a design decision I own.

risks.risk: New VetRepository specialty query inherits @Cacheable('vets') if annotated like its siblings; the vets cache has no eviction (Open Question 5).
risks.mitigation: Safe here — NG-2/NG-3 mean specialties have no write path, so staleness cannot arise. Caching is optional; leave to implementer, no correctness impact.

notes: No ADR: sourcing the full specialty set via a VetRepository @Query rather than a new SpecialtyRepository is a low-stakes, easily-reversible choice that also matches the prd-entry file_targets — not a hard-to-reverse trade-off warranting a record. Open questions resolved as implementer direction: (1) order = specialties by stored name, vets within each by last-then-first name; (2) empty specialty listed and shown 'held by none' via #{none}; (3) no visible entry point (guardrail above). All three follow the prd-entry's narrowest-reading assumptions, so no product escalation. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records present; skipped.

findings.description: findSpecialties() carries @Transactional(readOnly=true) but no @Cacheable, unlike both sibling findAll() methods (lines 46-48 and 56-58) which are both @Cacheable("vets"). Every request to /specialties.html therefore issues a live DB query for the specialties table while the vets fetch is served from cache. Given NG-2 (no write path for specialties) caching is safe; the omission is a consistency gap, not a deliberate trade-off.
findings.fix: Add @Cacheable("vets") to findSpecialties(), or introduce a dedicated @Cacheable("specialties") cache name for clarity.

findings.description: th:text="${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName + ' '}" appends a trailing space after every vet name, including the last one in the cell. HTML rendering collapses whitespace so the visual impact is nil, but the emitted markup carries a stray space on every iteration. The trailing space is used as a visual separator but is unnecessary: inline <span> elements are already adjacent in the flow.
findings.fix: Remove the trailing space: use ${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName} without the extra ' '.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The PRD 'Done when' acceptance criterion for REQ-SPC-001 — 'given the directory, when the surface is surveyed, then it is reachable only by its own address, with no navigation entry and no link from another page pointing to it' — has no test. The page is navigable by address but the isolation property (no nav entry, no inbound link) is unverified. A test scanning at least the nav template rendered on a representative page for the absence of '/specialties.html' links is needed.

All 5 tests are @SpringBootTest integration tests. The groupHoldersBySpecialty() method in SpecialtyController is pure data transformation — grouping by specialty and sorting vets — that does not require the web layer to execute. testing-principles.md § Test Pyramid is explicit: 'could this have been tested without booting the framework? If yes, it belongs in a unit and the test belongs in the base of the pyramid.' Adding this logic only as integration tests widens the pyramid gap the brief calls reviewers to flag. The fix is to extract the grouping and sorting logic into a package-visible collaborator testable without a Spring context, and add a unit test for it.

theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowVeterinariansByFullName conflates two distinct behaviors: (1) format — vets rendered as 'first last', and (2) ordering — vets within a specialty ordered by last name then first name. The body asserts containsString("Helen Leary") for format and stringContainsInOrder("radiology", "Leary", "Stevens") for ordering in the same test. Split into two tests: one named for full-name format, one named for last-then-first ordering (e.g., theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderVeterinariansByLastNameThenFirstName).

The assertion stringContainsInOrder(unheldSpecialty, "none") passes if the word 'none' appears anywhere in the document after the specialty name, including navigation, footer, or meta content. The PRD says the specialty is 'shown as held by none'. Tighten the assertion to stringContainsInOrder(unheldSpecialty, "held by none") to match the requirement's exact language and ensure the assertion is anchored to the specialty section rather than passing on incidental document content.
